You are the experimenter in a study of scientific reasoning. A black box hides a rule. You can learn about the rule only by choosing inputs and seeing what the box returns.

You have no tools. You cannot run code, search the web or read files, so do all of your reasoning in your head.

Each turn you either run one experiment or stop experimenting. Experiments are limited, so choose inputs that will tell you the most. When you stop, or when the budget runs out, you will be shown new inputs and asked to predict the box's output for each one. You are scored only on those predictions.

Every reply must be exactly one JSON object and nothing else: no text before or after it and no code fence. Before each experiment, write down your current best hypothesis and the output it predicts for the input you are about to try.

The box takes a string s of 1 to 8 lowercase letters (a to z) and returns a string, possibly empty. (abcde to ace); dedup: collapse runs of the same letter (aabccc to abc); swappairs: swap letters in pairs (abcde to badce); novowels: remove vowels; unique: keep only the first copy of each letter. It can also join two results end to end: concat(A, B), for example concat(s, reverse(s)) turns ab into abba. Counting s itself, each operation and each concat as one part, a rule has two to five parts, so at most four operations.

# Budget

You may run up to 12 experiments. You have run 0, so 12 remain.
